title: How Does an AI Model Work?
audience: Clinical researchers and clinician-scientists new to AI
objectives: Place current AI capabilities in historical context using the interactive timeline.
Test a personal belief about AI against evidence and read the structured verdict.
Follow a deployed clinical model through its lifecycle and recognise data drift.
Decide when a performance drop justifies retraining.
Validate incoming records against acceptable ranges before inference.

sections.name: Interactive AI Timeline
sections.purpose: Place today's capabilities in historical context.
sections.how_to_use: Scroll the embedded timeline from Turing in the 1950s through generative models in the 2020s.

sections.name: AI: Fact or Fiction?
sections.purpose: Test a belief about AI against evidence.
sections.how_to_use: Type any statement about AI into the text box and press Enter. The verdict appears with six expandable panels (real-world applications, limitations, research opportunities, AI concepts, datasets, further reading). Requires NAVIGATOR_TOOLKIT_API_KEY; without it the input is disabled and a notice explains why.

sections.name: The AI Lifecycle in Deployment
sections.purpose: Follow a model the hospital deployed two years ago, whose risk flags a nurse now says feel off, and see what happened to it.
sections.how_to_use: Pick a model version and an incoming data batch. Deployment v3 contains drift. Compare accuracy, ROC-AUC, the confusion matrix, and the predicted-probability histogram. Run Model v1 across all three batches to find where it first drops, then run Model v3 on batch 3 to see whether retraining recovers it.

sections.name: Data validation
sections.purpose: Catch bad records before they become predictions.
sections.how_to_use: Four range sliders (age, systolic BP, cholesterol, BMI) check ten sampled records. Records outside every range are flagged for review.

chatbot_guidance: This subsection publishes the Fact-or-Fiction verdict to the AI Guide as live state, so you can refer to the learner's most recent statement and verdict directly.
If the learner asks why accuracy dropped, steer them to the difference between the model version and the data batch rather than to the code.
Emphasise that drift is not a bug: the model is unchanged and the population moved.
Every chart on this page has a 'View chart data as text (accessible alternative)' expander beneath it, holding the same numbers as a table.
